docTitle: LinkedIn carousel: Don't be cruel to AI. But not because it's conscious.

slides.title:
Don’t be cruel
to AI. But not
because it’s
==conscious.==
slides.sub:
From Nov 12, 2026, Anthropic bans sustained, needless cruelty to its AI, Claude. I’m all for kindness.
I question the reason.

slides.title: The rule
slides.takeaway:
It bans “sustained and needless” cruelty toward its AI models, including Claude.
*From November 12, 2026.*

sides.t: Common frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, model testing and research.
Users who repeatedly act cruelly, with no discernible purpose. Only extreme cases.

slides.title: If someone keeps going

chat.text: I SAID DO IT, YOU STUPID BOT

slides.input: You can start a new chat
slides.takeaway: Ending the chat is the main way it’s enforced. No account bans have been announced.

slides.title: The reasoning
slides.lede: The rule never mentions consciousness. Claude’s constitution says:
slides.note: Anthropic calls Claude’s moral status “deeply uncertain”. It hasn’t said Claude is conscious.

lines: It is not a human. It is an incredibly amazing tool.
Consciousness belongs to living things, not to a model, not to an algorithm.

slides.title: A slippery slope
slides.quote: “We must build AI for people; not to be a digital person.”
slides.her: We are assigning human attributes to a tool that does not possess human attributes… So I don’t see how this is going to end nicely.

slides.title: Follow the logic
slides.her: Does that mean that at some point Claude can have the ability to say… “Hey, I’m tired. I don’t want to do anything else”?
slides.takeaway: And if it could, what would that make the company using it day and night?

slides.title:
Be kind
for your
own sake.
slides.body: We should just not be cruel because we don’t want to be cruel people.

slides.title:
Where do
you draw
the line?
slides.ask: A powerful tool, or something that deserves protection? I’d like to hear your view.
slides.video: Claude Can End Your Chat If You’re Cruel. But Why?
